subject.title: fix(cost): align token usage refresh cadence with global settings

question: Should potentially expensive token/cost scans inherit the global refresh cadence—including one-minute and live Adaptive intervals—or retain an explicit slower cost-scan policy?
rationale: Current behavior and UI define an hourly cost cadence, while this PR intentionally changes that default and may materially increase local scanning work; tests cannot determine the desired product and battery-performance tradeoff.

options.title: Expose a cost-scan cadence
options.body: Keep token/cost scheduling explicit with a separate setting or documented minimum while preserving immediate forced refreshes and the PR's scheduling safety fixes.

options.title: Approve global inheritance
options.body: Let token/cost scans follow every global cadence after the contributor demonstrates acceptable real-corpus CPU, disk, battery, timeout, and setting-transition behavior.

options.title: Retain hourly behavior
options.body: Close the linked request and keep the current hourly cost policy if protecting local resources outweighs cadence consistency.

recommendation.title: Expose a cost-scan cadence
recommendation.body: Keep token/cost scheduling explicit with a separate setting or documented minimum while preserving immediate forced refreshes and the PR's scheduling safety fixes.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available owner for the cost-usage feature and its refresh-policy tradeoff.
